subsystems.role: bipedal walking, balancing and recovery on uneven floors.

subsystems.name: Actuators
subsystems.role: electric motors and gearboxes that move every joint with enough torque and speed.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: stores and manages energy for a few hours of work.

subsystems.name: Manipulation
subsystems.role: arms and end effectors that pick up totes, boxes or parts.

subsystems.name: Perception and sensing
subsystems.role: lets the robot see its surroundings, locate objects and feel contact.

subsystems.role: runs walking controllers and learned task policies on board.

subsystems.name: Safety system
subsystems.role: keeps people around the robot safe during supervised trials.

buildSteps.title: Choose a task and a safety envelope
buildSteps.detail: Pilots start with one repetitive job, such as moving totes between a conveyor and a pallet, so the robot only needs a narrow set of skills.

buildSteps.title: Design the kinematics
buildSteps.detail: Engineers fix the number of joints, limb lengths and range of motion so the robot can reach the work without being unnecessarily heavy.

buildSteps.title: Make the actuators and joints
buildSteps.detail: Motors, gearboxes, bearings and encoders are assembled into compact joint modules that can be swapped out quickly.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the structure
buildSteps.detail: Legs, arms and torso are machined or cast from aluminium or moulded from carbon fibre to keep weight down.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power, sensors and computing
buildSteps.detail: Batteries, cameras, force sensors and the control computer are wired into the frame and the robot is balanced and calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Train control policies
buildSteps.detail: Walking is tuned with model-based controllers, while manipulation tasks are learned from teleoperation and simulation using imitation learning.

buildSteps.title: Test in the lab
buildSteps.detail: The robot repeats the task thousands of times, including recovering from falls and handling misplaced objects.

buildSteps.title: Run supervised pilots
buildSteps.detail: The robot works alongside people at a real site, with remote operators ready to take over, collecting data that feeds the next software version.

buildSteps.title: Iterate and start volume production
buildSteps.detail: Hardware and software are refined together, and manufacturing moves from hand-built prototypes toward assembly lines.

prerequisites.why: humanoids need strong, light joints; electric motors with high-ratio gearboxes now make this possible.

prerequisites.tech: Batteries with enough energy for a shift
prerequisites.why: current lithium-ion packs give only a few hours of heavy work, so most pilots run short shifts or swap batteries.
vision-language-action models let robots generalise to new objects, but they are still unreliable over long periods.
training in physics simulators lets robots learn skills without damaging real hardware.
simple grippers work for totes, but human-level manipulation remains hard.

prerequisites.tech: Safety standards for legged collaborative robots
prerequisites.why: existing factory robot rules assume fixed machines, so humanoid pilots use extra supervision.

pathway.milestone: supervised single-task pilots in warehouses and factories, such as moving bins or loading parts
pathway.unlocks: real-world data and proof that the hardware survives a working day.

pathway.milestone: commercial deployments of one or two tasks with remote human backup
pathway.unlocks: a business case based on filling labour gaps rather than replacing whole jobs.

pathway.milestone: multi-task robots that switch jobs with software updates
pathway.unlocks: wider use in logistics, manufacturing and hazardous work.

pathway.milestone: safe, general-purpose humanoids working among people without close supervision
pathway.unlocks: use in homes, care settings and small businesses, if reliability and cost allow.
